analysis:
The only change in this PR is a one-line documentation edit in docs/reference/configuration.md (line 410). It extends the description of DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK so that it also lists provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/ClusterServiceCommand.swift (supervisorConfiguration) as a reader and says the variable skips the darkbloom cluster pair's update at its slot. The two supplied units (lines 676-949 and 950-1216) are unchanged base text from the same file. They cover the prefix-cache, cluster and approval configuration reference and are not touched by the patch. No code, defaults, permissions, wire contracts or threat-model controls change.

Security relevance: the variable only suppresses update checks and is a local operator-controlled environment switch. It is not an attestation, authorization or encryption control. Skipping the update at the cluster slot lets an operator hold back a build, which relates to the existing watchdog/update surface (T-043) but widens nothing the operator could not already do. The operator is the already-adversarial local party (ADV-001). The environment variable is read from the process's own environment, and I saw no evidence that the coordinator or a peer can set it.

Open question for integration, which I could not verify from the supplied text: whether ClusterServiceCommand.swift actually honors the variable as documented, and whether skipping a cluster update interacts with the native-runtime approval digest pinning in the cluster sections. That pinning is described in unchanged text. Without ClusterServiceCommand.swift I cannot confirm the documentation matches the code, but a doc-only edit creates no regression. The patch excerpt is marked incomplete, but changed_ranges shows only line 410 changed. I found no regression and nothing needs updating in the threat model.
